_meta.rule: HOTLINES: NEVER add or edit a hotline/text-line number without a human verifying it against an authoritative source (source=national_verified, verified=true). A wrong crisis number is catastrophically worse than the directory fallback.

emergency_south_korea_119.name: Emergency services
emergency_south_korea_119.validation_notes: CITED 2026-10-29 (CIRISAgent#1248) under the owner's cited-sources standard (>=2 independent agreeing sources, >=1 official; no human check). Sources: UK FCDO travel advice: UK FCDO travel advice, Getting help: "Emergency services in South Korea Ambulance: 119 Fire: 119 Police: 112" (fetched 2026-10-29 via gov.uk content API) | National Archives of Korea (국가기록원): "119번으로 신고를 하면 소방차와 앰뷸런스가 출동하여 긴급구조를 해준다고 생각하는 것이다. 119번은 원래 화재신고 번호였다. 그러다가 몇 차례의 대형 재난사고가 발생한 후 각종 긴급구조 전화번호를 119번으로 통일해서 화재를 포함하여 각종 긴급구조 상황 발생할 때 신고하도록 하고 있다." (https://theme.archives.go.kr/next/koreaOfRecord/119.do) | AOSP eccdata (Android's emergency-number database): KR 119 types ['FIRE']. Sources agree it reaches: ambulance, fire. Listed beyond that by some sources only: police. UK FCDO page checked: https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/south-korea/getting-help (fetched 2026-10-29); page text: UK FCDO travel advice, Getting help: "Emergency services in South Korea Ambulance: 119 Fire: 119 Police: 112" (fetched 2026-10-29 via gov.uk content API). Cross-check (not a source): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_emergency_telephone_numbers — wikipedia agrees. 'languages' = the locale this entry is staged for (ko), not a verified statement of operator languages.
